lines: Two-channel counterpoint sequencer: each of four stages carries a slider for channel A and one for channel B, and a trigger flips which of the two that stage feeds
Adds its setting to the A output while that stage is flipped to channel A, 0V fully down to 1.25V fully up, or 2V with the wider range chosen for channel A
Adds its setting to the B output while that stage is flipped to channel B, 0V fully down to 1.25V fully up, or 2V with the wider range chosen for channel B
Flips all four stages away from channel A on a rising edge above 2V, leaving the A output at 0V and the B output carrying all four of its sliders
Flips all four stages away from channel B on a rising edge above 2V, leaving the B output at 0V and the A output carrying all four of its sliders
Flips the first stage between channel A and channel B on each rising edge above 2V
Flips that stage between channel A and channel B on each rising edge above 2V; with no cable in it, the stage is flipped by every second trigger of the stage before it
The sum of the A sliders of whichever stages are flipped to channel A, so 0V to 5V, or 0V to 8V with the wider range chosen for channel A
The sum of the B sliders of whichever stages are flipped to channel B, so 0V to 5V, or 0V to 8V with the wider range chosen for channel B
Menu — 2V range for channel A — makes each of channel A's four sliders span 0V to 2V in place of 0V to 1.25V, so the A output reaches 8V
Menu — 2V range for channel B — makes each of channel B's four sliders span 0V to 2V in place of 0V to 1.25V, so the B output reaches 8V
Note — every stage comes up flipped to channel B, so the A output starts at 0V and the B output carries all four of its sliders
Note — a stage feeds one channel or the other and never both, so the two outputs together always carry the same set of four stages divided between them
Note — the lamp in a slider lights while that stage is feeding that channel, and the two lamps by the outputs brighten with the voltage each output is carrying
Note — on a sample where either reset jack fires, the stage triggers are not read at all, so a trigger arriving at the same moment as a reset is lost

Aristotle.notes: Params 0 and 1 hold the two voltage-range menu settings and have no widget, so no click reaches them. The stage counters are divide-by-two: a stage passes a high level on to the next stage's normalled trigger every second trigger it receives (src/tools/InsAndOuts.hpp:106-124), which makes the four stages a binary ripple counter when no trigger cables are patched past the first. The output range figure of 0 to 8V is the wider setting; the default range gives 0 to 5V.

Medusa.notes: The mix is a plain weighted sum, input 1 times (6 minus the output index) over 6 plus input 2 times the output index over 6 (src/Medusa.cpp:33), and nothing clamps it, so two 10V inputs give 10V out and larger inputs pass straight through. The ports are given the cv family because the panel itself prints CV IN on both inputs; the module would pass audio just as happily.

Eris.notes: No family is given to any of these ports: the matrix carries whatever is patched into it, audio or control voltage, and the panel says nothing either way. The trimpot at a given panel position is param (row + 4 times column), where the row is the input letter and the column is the output number (src/Eris.cpp:87-89); the maker's own configParam numbering is input plus 4 times output, which comes to the same thing. Param 17 is the aux gain menu setting and has no widget. The four numbered outputs are configured with the names 0 to 3 (src/Eris.cpp:22) while the panel prints 1 to 4. The vactrol's own source comments say the ramps are 6ms and 60ms, while the constants in the same function are 0.00125 and 0.0125 seconds (src/Vactrol.hpp:44-51); the constants are what runs.
